summary: The change hits the intended sqrt(eta) slope regime, but I do not think it is ready to merge as a claimed Ma-Zeng-Zhou 2018 Appendix-B first pass. The main path uses a different Z-basis error model than the paper, and the phase-error helper can stop being a conservative upper bound when callers provide `Y_1`. The current tests are too loose to catch either problem. I verified this by reading the patch and local paper/spec excerpts; I could not execute `pytest` in this sandbox because there is no writable temp directory.

issues.description: `pm_bit_error_rate` is documented as the Ma §V / Appendix-B honest-behavior simulation, but it does not implement the paper's QBER model. Appendix B uses Eq. (B19)/(B22), i.e. an `e_δ(M)`-based term with an `exp(-ημ)` factor, whereas this code uses a BB84-style mixture `[(Q_μ-Y_0)e_d + Y_0/2]/Q_μ`. Under the default operating point this materially changes the rate: at 50 dB, this path gives `E_Z≈1.56e-2`, while the paper-model approximation is `≈4.33e-3`, shrinking `R` by about 4.6x.
issues.suggestion: Either implement the Appendix-B model directly (B19/B22, with the phase-slice misalignment term) or rename/document this as a separate approximation instead of citing it as the Ma Fig. 3b / Appendix-B simulation.

issues.description: `pm_phase_error_upper` is only conservative on the default path because the internal fallback `Y_1 = (Q_μ - Y_0)/μ` happens to understate the honest `Y_1`. The public `Y_1` override is unconstrained, so a caller can pass an optimistic yield and silently lower the returned 'upper bound'. For example, at `μ=0.3` and `η_channel=1e-3`, increasing `Y_1` by 10% drops `E_X` from about `0.27` to about `0.20`. For a bound helper, that is unsafe behavior.
issues.suggestion: Make the parameter explicitly a lower bound (for example `Y_1_lower`), validate the implied `q_1`, or remove the override until a real decoy lower bound exists. If you keep the Appendix-B-style first pass, also cap the phase-error value at `0.5` before feeding it into entropy, as the paper's simulation code does.

issues.description: The test file never pins `pm_bit_error_rate` to the Appendix-B QBER formula and never checks the safety property that makes the default `pm_phase_error_upper` path conservative (namely, that the fallback `Y_1` does not exceed the honest-behavior `Y_1`). That is why materially different 'honest simulation' formulas still pass all 20 tests.
issues.suggestion: Add formula-pinned regression tests for B19/B20/B22/B27, or at minimum a couple of fixed operating-point checks against the paper-model approximations plus a test that the fallback `Y_1` stays below `pm_single_photon_yield` over the supported regime.

issues.description: The module docstring and the `TestPmCharlieGain` class comment describe `Q_μ` with a squared factor (`2*(1-(1-p_d)e^{-ημ/2})^2*e^{-ημ/2}`), but the implementation uses `2*fire*silent`. That inconsistency will mislead future maintenance, especially because the paper's Appendix-B approximation is a third expression again.
issues.suggestion: Update the docstrings/comments so they match the actual implemented gain formula and state explicitly whether it is the exact one-click model or the Appendix-B approximation.

round_recommendation: Fix the Z-basis error model first, then harden `pm_phase_error_upper` so it cannot become non-conservative via `Y_1`, and add formula-pinned tests for those two helpers before re-review.
